new_entities.name: Methotrexate without folic acid supplementation
new_entities.description: Methotrexate treatment given without routine folic or folinic acid supplementation.

new_entities.name: Mucositis and alopecia
new_entities.description: Mucocutaneous toxic effects such as stomatitis, oral ulceration, and hair loss during methotrexate treatment.

edges.effect_quant: A meta-analysis of randomized trials found folic acid reduced mucosal and gastrointestinal toxicity with an OR of 0.21, implying substantially higher mucocutaneous toxicity when methotrexate is used without folate supplementation.
edges.population: adults receiving low-dose methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis and similar inflammatory disorders
edges.mechanism: Methotrexate antagonizes folate-dependent cellular replication, and tissues with high turnover such as oral mucosa and hair follicles are especially vulnerable when exogenous folate replacement is absent.
edges.summary: Using low-dose methotrexate without folic acid meaningfully increases the likelihood of mucocutaneous toxicity, especially stomatitis and related oral ulcer symptoms. The overall evidence base is consistent enough that routine folate co-prescription has become standard practice.
edges.caveats: Most controlled data come from rheumatoid arthritis populations, with mucosal and gastrointestinal outcomes more directly measured than alopecia in isolation. The edge is therefore strongest for mouth-ulcer and broader mucocutaneous toxicity rather than for hair loss alone.

evidence.citation: Ortiz Z et al 1998 J Rheumatol
evidence.notes: The efficacy of folic acid and folinic acid in reducing methotrexate gastrointestinal toxicity in rheumatoid arthritis. A metaanalysis of randomized controlled trials.

effect_quant.comparator: approximate inverse of the folic-acid-protective OR 0.21, reflecting greater mucosal and GI toxicity without folate supplementation

evidence.citation: Shea B et al 2013 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
evidence.notes: Folic acid and folinic acid for reducing side effects in patients receiving methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis.

effect_quant.comparator: approximate inverse of the 26% relative risk reduction in gastrointestinal side effects seen with folate supplementation

evidence.citation: Mazaud C et al 2017 Br J Dermatol
evidence.notes: Relative risk of and determinants for adverse events of methotrexate prescribed at a low dose: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials.
